newsitem.title: UK: Antofagasta sells mine stake for $256 mln.
newsitem.headline: Antofagasta sells mine stake for $256 mln.

text.p: London-listed Antofagasta Holdings Plc said on Friday it agreed to sell a 40 percent stake in Chile's Los Pelambres copper mine to two Japanese groups for about $256 million in cash.

The first consortium, which included Nippon Mining & Metals Co Ltd, Marubeni Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd, planned to buy a 25 percent stake, while companies owned by the second group would hold a 15 percent equity interest.
The second Japanese group included Mitsubishi Materials Corp and Mitsubishi Corp.

In addition, Nippon Mining and Mitsubishi Materials conditionally agreed to buy 400,000 tonnes per year of copper concentrates from the project on a long-term basis of about 12 years, Antofagasta said in a statement.
Antofagasta is owned by Chile's Luksic group.
The company said it would use proceeds from the deal to fund its equity financing obligations related to its 60 percent stake in the project.
Development costs for the project were estimated at about $1.3 billion.

Antofagasta projected planned production from Los Pelambres for the first 10 years at an average of 743,000 tonnes per year of copper concentrates, yielding about 246,000 tonnes per year of fine copper.
Antofagasta's shares rose 3.5p to 398.5 by 0745 GMT. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
